name: Chart Select (CALL Pulse)
summary: A CALL-only rise/fall pulse that runs on a shared Deriv demo account. You can watch every trade, win or lose, on the live board.
rule: Scan selected volatility charts for RSI(14) at or below 38.
Enter a CALL only when RSI turns up and the candle closes green.
Default demo stake is $0.35; $1 only on 1HZ25V 10m.
Markets that drained the demo book are sat out. No PUT book.

risk.perTrade: Fixed small demo stake on every trade.
risk.stop: Each rise/fall contract has a fixed stake, so the most one trade can lose is that stake.
risk.dailyStop: Practice funds only. No real money is traded on this desk.

breakEvenNote: A winning rise/fall contract pays less than the stake it risks, so the break-even win rate sits around 53-56%. Win rate alone says nothing until you compare it with that bar.
limits: The timeframes per market were picked from a 90-day replay. That is in-sample, so the live board is the real test, not the replay.
Demo fills are not real fills. Live results can differ.
A positive demo run does not mean you will make money with real funds.

name: Gold H1 Trend
summary: A simple trend-following strategy for gold on the H1 chart. It is paper-tested live on this site: every simulated trade, win or lose, is published.
rule: Trade only in the direction of the 200 EMA.
Enter when the 20 EMA crosses the 50 EMA on a closed H1 candle.
Stop-loss at 2x ATR(14). Take-profit at 2x the stop distance.
One position at a time. No martingale, no grid, no averaging down.

risk.perTrade: Results are measured in R (1R is the distance from entry to stop). The MT5 version risks 1% of balance per trade.
risk.stop: Every trade has a hard stop-loss at 2x ATR.
risk.dailyStop: The MT5 version stops after a 3% daily closed loss. The paper test does not model a daily limit.

breakEvenNote: With a 2:1 reward-to-risk target the strategy needs to win roughly one trade in three to break even before costs. Spread and slippage on gold push that bar higher.
limits: The record is simulated on candle data with an assumed spread. No MT5 or live-account record exists yet.
Trend-following strategies lose often in ranging markets. Expect long losing streaks.
Results only mean something after at least 100 trades, which can take many months at this strategy's pace.

name: Gold London Breakout
summary: Trades the break of the Asian-session range on gold during the London morning. Paper-tested live, with every simulated trade published.
rule: Mark the high and low of the 00:00-07:00 UTC session.
Skip the day if that range is narrower than 0.5x or wider than 3x ATR(14).
Enter when an H1 candle opening between 07:00 and 10:00 UTC closes beyond the range: long above the high, short below the low.
Stop-loss at the other side of the range. Take-profit at 1.5x the stop distance.
Close any open trade at 20:00 UTC. One trade per day.

risk.perTrade: Results are measured in R (1R is the distance from entry to stop). Size any real trade so that 1R is a small fixed share of your balance.
risk.stop: Every trade has a hard stop-loss at the opposite side of the range.
risk.dailyStop: One trade per day at most. No other daily limit is modelled.

breakEvenNote: With a 1.5:1 reward-to-risk target the strategy needs to win about 40% of trades to break even, before spread.
limits: False breakouts are common at the London open.
Gold spreads widen around news, so the assumed spread may be too low at the moments this strategy trades.
Fixed UTC session times ignore daylight-saving shifts in when London opens.
The record is simulated on candle data. Real fills will differ.

name: Forex Breakout and Retest
summary: Waits for a 20-candle breakout, then only enters if price retests the broken level and holds. Paper-tested live on three major pairs.
rule: A breakout is an H1 candle that closes beyond the high (or low) of the previous 20 candles.
Within the next 5 candles, enter only if price pulls back to within 0.25 ATR of the broken level and closes back on the breakout side.
Trade only in the direction of the 100 EMA.
Stop-loss 0.5 ATR beyond the retest extreme or the level. Take-profit at 2x the stop distance.
Each breakout is traded at most once.

risk.perTrade: Results are measured in R (1R is the distance from entry to stop). Size any real trade so that 1R is a small fixed share of your balance.
risk.stop: Every trade has a hard stop-loss.
risk.dailyStop: No daily limit is modelled in the paper test. Add one if you ever trade it for real.

breakEvenNote: With a 2:1 reward-to-risk target the strategy needs to win roughly one trade in three to break even, and spread costs raise that bar.
limits: Breakout strategies lose often in choppy, ranging markets.
The three pairs often move together, so their trades are not fully independent.
The record is simulated on candle data with assumed spreads. Real fills, slippage and requotes will be worse.
The rules were fixed before any results and not tuned on data. Any change starts a new record.

name: Forex RSI/Bollinger Reversion
summary: Fades stretched moves back toward the average, only when the market is not trending. Paper-tested live on three major pairs.
rule: Only trade when ADX(14) is below 20, meaning the market is not trending.
Buy when an H1 candle closes below the lower Bollinger Band (20, 2) with RSI(14) under 30. Sell on the mirror image above the upper band with RSI above 70.
The target is the middle band (the 20-candle average) at the time of the signal.
Stop-loss at 1.5x ATR(14) from entry.

risk.perTrade: Results are measured in R (1R is the distance from entry to stop). Size any real trade so that 1R is a small fixed share of your balance.
risk.stop: Every trade has a hard stop-loss at 1.5x ATR.
risk.dailyStop: No daily limit is modelled in the paper test. Add one if you ever trade it for real.

breakEvenNote: In backtests on 2017 to 2026 Deriv data the target was usually about twice as far from entry as the stop, so the break-even win rate is about one trade in three. The backtested win rate was 31%, just under that bar, and the strategy lost money after costs.
limits: Mean reversion works until a trend starts. A strong breakout can produce a run of full-size losses.
It trades rarely, so a meaningful sample can take a year or more.
The record is simulated on candle data with assumed spreads. Real fills will differ.
The rules were fixed before any results and not tuned on data. Any change starts a new record.
